findings.quote: The conductor must be connected to the ground, so electrons can flow to or from it.
findings.problem: This is a false absolute. Charging by induction does not need a ground. Two neutral metal spheres in contact, with a charged rod brought near and the spheres separated before the rod is removed, each end with a net charge and no ground is used. A student taught that a ground is required will answer that the spheres stay neutral, which is wrong. The round-1 finding itself said grounded or split. The brief lists charging mechanisms at official curriculum class (dost-sei-L054).
findings.source: OpenStax College Physics for AP Courses, section 18.2 Conductors and Insulators, Figure 18.13 (two spheres in contact, separated before the rod is removed, retain net charges) and Figure 18.14 (grounding): https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-ap-courses/pages/18-2-conductors-and-insulators; reader-rules.md, Added after the Sol audit
